Curiosity is a way of working

I grew up in a small North Carolina town, moving between Spanish and English, home and school, and later science and business. It taught me to notice what gets lost between perspectives and to look for the connection.

In the souk in Fez, vendors read a customer before they name a price. Analysts do something similar with companies: they read the numbers and the story together before they make a call. I want to get good at that kind of reading.

Finance interests me as a way to study how organizations grow, allocate resources and create lasting value, especially in emerging markets. What I'm missing is the technical training to back up my instincts.

Outside of class I'm the person who says yes to the dish most people hesitate over: babbouche in Morocco, haggis in Edinburgh, fried crickets in Mexico. I try to meet new ideas the same way.

Learning by doing the work

Investing, research, entrepreneurship and leadership.

From sourcing to pitch in eight weeks

Investing, Girls in Venture Capital

I sourced, evaluated and pitched a seed-stage investment thesis, running due diligence, market analysis and competitive landscape research. I evaluated three opportunities and presented my findings to Visible Ventures. It taught me to read a company's numbers and its story together until I could commit to a conclusion.

A funded idea, from prototype to pitch

Entrepreneurship, high school

I saw a tradeoff many families face between healthier eating and the food that ties them to their culture. So I built an app concept that reimagines traditional dishes with healthier ingredients. After months of research, development and a working prototype, I pitched it to a panel at the Grant Cardone Foundation and received $4,000 in funding to keep developing it.

Writing to Washington about Morocco

Policy research, Duke in the Arab World

I wrote a 5-page policy memo to the U.S. Department of State on civic space suppression in Morocco. It cites 10+ statistical and institutional sources and makes three evidence-based recommendations.

Research that works in every language

Research, Duke Culture Lab

I built and maintain 16 lab web pages across 6 projects, resolved 100+ design and data errors in survey logic for 5 studies, and translate study materials into Spanish. That helps a cross-cultural study reach a projected 800+ participants across four continents.

Getting ten students to Mexico

Leadership, Duke Catholic Center

As mission trip coordinator, I led a 7-month planning process to select 10 students and organize flights, lodging and logistics with Universidad Anáhuac, so we could serve the community of Santa María de la Mexicana.

Questions I'm carrying forward

What I'm learning right now.

How do investors evaluate markets that grow informally?

In the Fez souk, the same rug had a different price depending on who the vendor thought I was. Across Africa, informal activity makes up close to a third of GDP. I want to understand how firms make long-term bets in markets that price themselves precisely without a formal system telling them to.

What lets fintech step into those markets?

I'm drawn to private equity in emerging markets, especially where fintech is entering economies that already run on close reads of people and trust.

What turns an early idea into a durable business?

My seed-stage thesis and my own app pitch pushed me on market timing and competitive positioning. Next I want the accounting, valuation and LBO tools to test those instincts with numbers.
